items.title: Show HN: Three Emojis, a daily word puzzle for language learners
items.raw_excerpt: I'm in the process of learning German and wanted to play a German version of the NYT’s Spelling Bee. It was awful, I was very bad at it, it was not fun. So I built my own version of Spelling Bee meant for people like me. Three Emojis is a daily word game designed for language learners. You get seven letters and a list of blanked-out words to find. When you discover shorter words, they automatically fill into longer ones—like a crossword—which turns out to be really useful for languages like German. Each word also gets three emojis assigned to it as a clue, created by GPT-5 to try and capture the word’s meaning (this works surprisingly well, most of the time). items.title: HOLO – a persistence framework that keeps AI context across resets

I’m looking for two or three engineers or researchers who’ve wrestled with context drift or continual-learning issues and want to test persistence models together.
Repo/demo available on request — this post is just to find the right people.
Holo.Simulations@gmail.com

items.title: GitChat – Branch AI chats on a canvas like Miro meets ChatGPT and Notion
items.raw_excerpt: I've been building GitChat as a side project to solve fragmented brainstorming in AI chats (linear threads bury ideas). So I wanted a non-linear space to visually connect thoughts. It's an AI chat app where you branch conversations across a dynamic canvas: pin websites, docs, images, and reference them in any thread for seamless collaboration. Think Miro's visual boards + ChatGPT's smarts + Notion's organization. Supports multiple AI modes (OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, Google, and more) Early beta, so expect rough edges; no mobile yet. Feedback welcome! Requires an invite code to get your account activated though. Lmk if you need one!
